# Quiet Growth

A mark for an emulator that grows past its origin without shouting about it. The philosophy is restraint with one deliberate transgression: every shape stays calm, geometric and centred, and exactly one element is allowed to leave the frame. That single crossing is the whole message, "extended", told by form instead of by a word.

Space is generous. The subject sits inside a stable enclosure, a ring or a block, with margins wide enough that the icon reads as a single silhouette at forty-eight pixels. Nothing decorative fills the gaps; the emptiness is what makes the crossing legible.

Colour is a night ground and one living hue. The ground is deep and slightly cool so the mark glows rather than sits; the living hue is a green-to-mint gradient that reads as growth on a dark screen and survives the flattening of small sizes. A second warm neutral may hold the enclosure, never a third colour.

Rhythm comes from strokes of equal weight and matching round terminals, so the composition feels drawn in one breath. Curves are few and long; corners are rounded on the same radius everywhere. The result should look meticulously crafted, the product of many refinements by someone who has drawn hundreds of marks and kept only the essential lines.

Text does not appear inside the mark. The name lives beside it in the launcher and in the app, so the icon carries meaning through form alone.
